notes: Complete individual Tsar Cannon display: long patinated bronze barrel with genuinely open deep bore and closed breech, thick ringed muzzle, cast bands, paired trunnions and side lifting lugs. Complete dark cast-metal carriage with both large open-spoked wheels, hubs/axle, paired stepped cheeks and crossmembers, rear trail and small support roller, plus an original faceted front casting and geometric scroll/rosette relief. Low stone platform and four separate displayed cannonballs on their small occupied contact bed. Original abstract geometry replaces portraits, arms, lion faces, inscriptions and plaque text. Surrounding trees, chains/bollards, paths, churches, palaces and all native buildings stay independent; no functioning weapon or navigable interior is asserted. Two actually inspected ordinary whole-side/front-oblique photographs and the cached current standard PMTiles. East-facing muzzle direction is approximate with25-degree uncertainty. Hidden carriage inventory, internal bore/chamber, wheel ornament, lifting hardware and original geometric relief are simplified; no copied figures, arms, lion portrait, lettering or plaque. The lower ball partly hidden in the photographs is retained in the four-ball display. Exact historic paving, numerical LOD errors and physical-device timings remain unmeasured.
